I have lived on this land for many years and I know what it needs. My family and I will work these 13 hectares with our hoes as we always do, using manure from our cattle to feed the soil because chemical fertilizer is too costly and difficult for me to fetch at my age. We will plant the seeds we saved from the last harvest—cassava and sorghum grow well here together—and trust the rains that come from November to April. I am too old to manage spraying chemicals or watering the crops, so we will rely on the rain and the strength of our hands.
